title: Finite affine coefficient domains and normalized tensor and line counits
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $d\geq0$ put $X_d=\mathbf A^d_Y$ and $p_d:X_d\to Y$ [def-sbc-affine-space], with $X_0=Y$ and $p_0=1_Y$. Use the small pro-etale derived categories, derived pullback and tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the specified Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], compact supports [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$ and $\omega_f=Rf^!A_{\operatorname{target}(f)}$. The vector integration $t_f:Rf_!A_{\operatorname{source}(f)}(r)[2r]\to A_{\operatorname{target}(f)}$ for a rank-$r$ trivial bundle $f$ is [def-amb-vector-integration], realized on this site by [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]. Write $P_{f,H}:Lf^*H(r)[2r]\to Rf^!H$ for the exceptional transpose of $(1_H\otimes t_f)\Pi_{f;A(r)[2r],H}$, where $\Pi_{f;M,H}:Rf_!(Lf^*H\otimes M)\to H\otimes Rf_!M$ is the inverse of the canonical compactification projection [def-exchange-projection], with tensor symmetries inserted.

Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, meaning bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. It has a bounded constructible ordinary-etale representative $K^e$, with $\nu_Y^*K^e\cong K$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], having the same finite Tor interval. For any coordinate projection and any base factor obtained from $K$ by coordinate pullback, tensoring with finite locally free Tate lines and shifts, these factors likewise have bounded constructible etale representatives; pullback preserves the Tor interval, a Tate line preserves it, and a shift translates it. The source factors $A(r)[2r]$, their products and their affine-line compact-support images have bounded constructible etale representatives. The projection maps on these pairs are invertible. The same is true of the projection maps at $(A_{X_d}(d)[2d],K)$ and $(\omega_{p_d},K)$. All coordinate schemes and their finite-type projective compactifications are Noetherian of finite dimension, so the exceptional Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] apply to the bounded etale-origin sources in these calculations.

Let $L=A_{X_d}(d)[2d]$, $P=P_{p_d,A_Y}:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{p_d}$, and let $\theta_{p_d,K}:Lp_d^*K\otimes\omega_{p_d}\to Rp_d^!K$ be the counit-transposed tensor map [def-pur-co-smoothness](2). Under canonical Tate/shift reassociation the actual maps satisfy
$$\theta_{p_d,K}\circ(1\otimes P)=P_{p_d,K}.$$

For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $S$ and $f:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$, use $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$ and $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$. On the ordinary etale site the projective-line trace $t_q$ is [def-amb-p1-trace], using $A^{e}(1)=\mu^{e}_{\ell^r}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}A$ for any $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$. Put $I_S=t_q\circ Rq_*(j_!A^{e}(1)[2]\to A^{e}(1)[2])$. Let $F_1\dashv G_1$, $G_1H=f^*H(1)[2]$, be the actual affine-line adjunction obtained by composing open extension with the normalized projective-line adjunction [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. For every $H\in D^b_{ctf}(S,A)$ and its etale representative, its counit, after $F_1=Rf_!$, is
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{line}}_H=(1_H\otimes I_S)\Pi_{f;A(1)[2],H}.$$
The specified site comparisons identify this equality, its projection map and its transpose with the corresponding pro-etale maps. These maps are independent of $r$. The pro-etale transpose is exactly the displayed integration-defined affine-line map $\Gamma_{f,H}$; on $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$ it is [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], and this formula defines it for all $n\geq1$. At $d=0$ the tensor identity is the identity-adjunction formula; for $K=0$ and on empty schemes these are the unique zero-object maps.

source.place: Proof: finite-coefficient realization and tensor reassociation; affine-line normalization in the ordered orientations; returned steps 1,2,7,8,11,12

proof.text: Choose a Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $K$. The equivalence in [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] supplies $K^e$ and preserves precisely $[a,b]$: $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $A$ is finite, hence Noetherian. For any coordinate pullback use [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude]; for a finite Tate line use the finite-level interval assertion in [prop-weil-twist-preserves]. A cohomological shift $[s]$ replaces $[a,b]$ by $[a-s,b-s]$, since $H^i(C[s])=H^{i+s}(C)$. Applying the same comparison equivalence on each coordinate scheme gives bounded constructible ordinary-etale representatives with these intervals. The polynomial affine charts show that every coordinate scheme and each projective compactification in use is finite type over $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] they are Noetherian, and [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives finite dimension. Thus each chosen compactification has a bound required by [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2); its Hom bijection applies to bounded-below sources of etale origin, without claiming an adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale objects.

source.place: Tag 0963, lemma-pullback-ctf; coefficient-origin and interval comparisons as in the cited DAG statements

proof.text: The ordinary Tate powers are locally free rank one and commute with pullback by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; their shifts and products are therefore bounded constructible etale objects. For a coordinate line over a base $T$, [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] at $d=1$ identifies its compact-support image of $A(1)[2]$ with $A_T$ by its actual counit trace. Tensoring with an additional line pulled back from $T$ gives its corresponding twisted, shifted image: apply [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] with that base line, which is finite Tor, and the line source, which is bounded constructible. This also treats the line factors occurring in ordered products. For every coordinate pair of the statement, that same theorem applies with the source factor just described and the base factor from Step 1. In particular it applies to $(L,K)$. These are the canonical compactification projection maps, and their pro-etale realizations are the maps of [def-exchange-projection], not unspecified isomorphisms.

source.place: Finite-coefficient realization of the affine-coordinate calculation; projection maps before tensor reassociation

proof.text: For the trivial rank-$d$ vector bundle $p_d$, [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] at the ordinary-etale input $A_Y$ says that the transpose of integration is an isomorphism. The map comparison and transpose equation of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] carry this exact map to $P=P_{p_d,A_Y}:L\to\omega_{p_d}$. Thus $P$ is an isomorphism and supplies an etale-origin witness for $\omega_{p_d}$, with the bounded constructible representative of $L$. The finite compact-support projection theorem now applies also at $(\omega_{p_d},K)$; alternatively its invertibility follows by naturality from that at $(L,K)$ and the isomorphism $P$. The same comparison theorem identifies $P_{p_d,K}$ with the ordinary integration transpose on the representatives of Step 1. All the sources used below are consequently bounded etale-origin objects in the Hom bijections of Step 1.

source.place: Integration-defined vector-bundle purity, transported by the specified site comparison

proof.text:
Write $F=Rp_{d!}$, $t=t_{p_d}$, and $\epsilon=\varepsilon_{p_d,A_Y}$. By definition of transpose, $\epsilon\circ F(P)=t$. Naturality of the inverse projection in its source factor gives the typed equality
$$\Pi_{p_d;\omega_{p_d},K}\circ F(1\otimes P)=(1_K\otimes F(P))\circ\Pi_{p_d;L,K}.$$
Indeed the forward projections are composites of natural transformations in [def-exchange-projection]; multiply their naturality square on both sides by the inverses proved above. By [def-pur-co-smoothness](2), the transpose of $\theta_{p_d,K}\circ(1\otimes P)$ is therefore
$$(1_K\otimes\epsilon)\Pi_{p_d;\omega_{p_d},K}F(1\otimes P)=(1_K\otimes(\epsilon F(P)))\Pi_{p_d;L,K}=(1_K\otimes t)\Pi_{p_d;L,K}.$$
The last map defines the transpose of $P_{p_d,K}$. Injectivity of the Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] proves the required equality. Tensor symmetries, unitors and Tate/shift reassociations here are exactly those used to define $\Pi$ and $\theta$, so no orientation choice enters this calculation.

source.place: Tensor reassociation: counit-transpose calculation for the coefficient tensor map

proof.text:
On the ordinary etale site over $S$, use the actual line adjunction and normalization stated by [lem-pur-coordinate-line-adjunction]. Its hypotheses hold for the separated finite-type base $S$, all $n\ge1$, and every annihilating exponent $r$; in particular no ramification divisibility is required. It identifies $F_1$ with $Rf_!$, $G_1H$ with $f^*H(1)[2]$, and gives precisely
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{line}}_H=(1_H\otimes I_S)\Pi_{f;A(1)[2],H},\qquad I_S=t_q\circ Rq_*(j_!A^e(1)[2]\to A^e(1)[2]).$$
Thus this is the counit of the specified composed adjunction, with $t_q$ the normalized projective-line trace, including the extension-by-zero counit in the definition of $I_S$. Apply the last clauses of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison]: they identify the restricted trace, canonical projection and integration transpose on the two sites and assert independence of the annihilating exponent. Consequently the pro-etale transpose of this very equality is the integration-defined $\Gamma_{f,H}$. On the range of the original [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] the formulas agree term for term; for the other $n$ this same formula defines the claimed extension.

source.place: Displayed restricted trace and its integration-defined exceptional transpose; actual line adjunction supplied by the cited coordinate-line lemma

proof.text: At $d=0$, the affine tower uses the identity adjunction of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace]. Hence $t=1$, $P=1$ under unit identifications, and Step 4 becomes the identity-adjunction formula. If $K=0$ or $H=0$, all displayed source and target objects in their coefficient formulas are zero, and their morphisms are the unique zero morphisms. The same conclusion holds on an empty scheme, whose module-sheaf derived category has only the zero object. None of Steps 1--5 required a reduced base or a nonzero coefficient field; the finite rings $A_{E,n}$ at $n=1$ and at ramified values of $n$ meet exactly the same hypotheses.

source.place: Identity tower at dimension zero; zero objects and empty schemes
